note.note:
Subjective:
- Patient presents with a 3-day history of sore throat, fever, and malaise.
- Symptoms started gradually and have progressively worsened.
- Reports difficulty swallowing and mild ear pain on the right side.
- No cough or nasal congestion reported.
- Past medical history: no chronic illnesses reported; no previous surgeries.
- Medications: none currently.
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social history: non-smoker, occasional alcohol use.

Objective:
- Throat examination reveals erythematous and swollen tonsils with white exudates bilaterally.
- Tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy noted on the right side.
- Temperature recorded at 101.3°F (38.5°C).
- No skin rash or conjunctival injection.
- Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
- No nasal discharge or sinus tenderness.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute Pharyngitis:
   - Assessment: Likely bacterial pharyngitis, possibly Group A Streptococcal infection.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Viral pharyngitis (consistent)
     - Infectious mononucleosis (consistent, especially with lymphadenopathy)
     - Peritonsillar abscess (less likely given no trismus or uvular deviation)
   - Investigations planned:
     - Rapid antigen detection test for Group A Streptococcus
     - Throat culture if antigen test negative but suspicion remains
     - Consider monospot test if symptoms persist or worsen
   - Treatment planned:
     - Empiric initiation of oral amoxicillin (dose/route/frequency not documented)
     - Hydration and supportive care with analgesics and antipyretics
   - Relevant referrals:
     - ENT referral if no improvement or signs of abscess development

Quality checks:
- Allergies and medications were documented.
- No conflicts between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality was clear and comprehensive.
